headline: Executive order signed by President George W. Bush aimed at strengthening security at US laboratories that handle dangerous biological materials.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order directs the federal government to improve biosecurity at laboratories in the United States. Biosecurity means protecting dangerous germs and toxins from theft, misuse, or accidental release. No summary was provided, so the specific steps the order requires are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Laboratories that work with dangerous germs and toxins
who_it_affects.how: These labs may face reviews of, or changes to, the security rules they must follow.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that oversee laboratory safety and security
who_it_affects.how: These agencies are likely directed to take steps to strengthen lab biosecurity.

when_it_takes_effect: Executive orders usually take effect when signed, so likely January 9, 2009.
